wines.summary: Fixin sits just south of Marsannay; 'crais de chêne' refers to the chalky soils that give structure and minerality. Collotte's 2023 is generous and immediately likeable. A reliable appellation wine that rewards patience to 2032.

Hautes-Côtes de Nuits occupies elevated terrain west of the grand cru strip — honest, food-friendly Pinot Noir at village prices. The 2022 Burgundy vintage was warm and concentrated, yielding wines with real depth for the appellation. Drink 2024–2030.

wines.varietal: Cab Franc, Merlot, Malbec, Cab Sauv
wines.summary: Utah-based Château la Caille sources from Washington's Columbia Valley for this Bordeaux-inspired blend of Cab Franc, Merlot, Malbec, and Cab Sauv. The 2021 Columbia Valley vintage was excellent. An approachable proprietary red in a good drinking window now.

Concha y Toro's flagship single-vineyard Cabernet has been Chile's benchmark for four decades. The 2020 vintage was exceptional across Maipo Valley — arguably a decade highlight. Purchased at $18 vs. $150 market: the standout QPR bottle in this cellar.

RunRig is one of Australia's most celebrated wines — old-vine Barossa Shiraz co-fermented with Viognier, aged 30 months in French oak. The 2020 earned 97 points. Purchased at $18 vs. $244 market: the greatest QPR bottle in this cellar. Do not open before 2026.

Il Bosco is Cesari's single-vineyard Amarone from dried Corvina, Corvinone, and Rondinella grapes — a wine of great concentration and warmth. The 2018 Amarone vintage was rich and generous. Drinking well from 2023 through 2035 at an exceptional purchase price.

Gran Selezione is Chianti Classico's apex designation — single-vineyard Sangiovese aged minimum 30 months. Lamole di Lamole sits at high elevation in the Greve sub-zone, producing taut, mineral wines. The 2020 vintage was stellar. A genuine bargain at purchase price.

Bolgheri Superiore sits at the heart of the Super Tuscan world on Tuscany's Maremma coast. Campo Al Mare's Baia al Vento is a structured Bordeaux blend from this prestigious coastal appellation. The 2020 vintage delivered excellent balance. Drink 2024–2033.

Kirkland's Saint-Émilion Grand Cru is consistently among the best-value Bordeaux on the market, typically sourced from classified châteaux under the Kirkland label. The 2022 Bordeaux vintage was outstanding — one of the decade's best. Drink from 2025.

Kirkland's Pauillac is sourced from classified Médoc châteaux and offers legitimate Left Bank structure at a fraction of the label price. The 2023 Bordeaux vintage is highly anticipated. This wine needs 3–5 more years of bottle age — patience will be rewarded.

Rieussec is a First Growth Sauternes neighbour to d'Yquem, and 1988 was one of the great botrytis vintages. At 38 years old, this bottle is almost certainly at or past its window — richly oxidative amber gold with dried fruit and marmalade complexity. Open immediately; do not delay.

Château Gris is Albert Bichot's Monopole — sole ownership — of an 8.5-acre walled Premier Cru vineyard south-west of Nuits-Saint-Georges, planted on terraced slopes between 260–330m. The Pinot Noir here is the classified 1er cru wine (the Chardonnay on site does not carry Premier Cru status). Expect the elegance of NSG — red and black fruit, violet, subtle oak — with serious aging potential. Give it at least 2026.

Sablet is a Côtes du Rhône Villages commune near Gigondas producing structured GSM blends with garrigue and dark fruit. Domaine de Pasquiers is a reliable producer. The 2020 southern Rhône vintage was excellent. Drinking well now through 2028.

wines.varietal: Mencía, Graciano, Carignan, Grenache, Nero d'Avola
wines.summary: Hiyu Wine Farm operates biodynamically in the Columbia Gorge, crafting the Pacific Northwest's most idiosyncratic wines. Clochain is a single field planted to a wild mix of southern European varieties. Earthy, complex, and unlike anything else in this cellar. A genuine conversation piece.

Patagonia's cool, wind-swept vineyards produce Cabernet Sauvignon with freshness rarely found in warmer Argentine regions. Malma/Chacra is associated with the Incisa della Rocchetta family of Sassicaia fame. The 2024 is very young — give it a couple of years before opening.

Saumur Blanc is one of the Loire's finest Chenin Blanc appellations, and Clotilde Legrand is a quality grower making wines with genuine mineral tension. The 2021 Loire vintage produced wines of excellent balance and acidity. 'À l'Écart' (off the beaten path) is aptly named.

Domaine Labet is one of Jura's most acclaimed estates, farming biodynamically on the Revermont hillsides. 'Cuvée du Hasard' (cuvée of chance) is old-vine Chardonnay of extraordinary precision. The 2018 is drinking beautifully now — a genuinely special bottle for the adventurous palate.

A 50/50 Pinot Blanc and Chardonnay blend from K.P. Keller — widely considered Germany's greatest producer. Old vines grown on clay-loam over limestone and marl, fermented with indigenous yeasts in large barrels. More Chablis than Chassagne in character: flinty minerality, citrus, and a filigreed limestone throughline. Built for the cellar; drink 2024–2033.

Esprit de Leflaive is the négociant label of the prestigious Domaine Leflaive (Puligny-Montrachet). This Nuits-Saint-Georges shows the structured, earthy character of the appellation. The 2018 Burgundy vintage was warm and generous — drinking well now and through 2033.

Hammerling Wines makes traditional-method sparkling wines from Pinot Noir grown in Santa Lucia Highlands and Carmel Valley. Sunset Debris is a Brut Rosé with fine bubbles and vivid strawberry-cream character. A delightful California sparkler — drink within the next few years.

Bugey Cerdon is a méthode ancestrale sweet sparkling wine from the Ain département, made from Gamay and Poulsard. Lightly sweet, deeply pink, and bursting with fresh raspberry fruit. A charming, unique wine — drink young and cold. Do not cellar this.

Laherte Frères is a standout grower Champagne from the Côte des Blancs, making wines of exceptional purity and tension. This Blanc de Blancs Brut Nature (zero dosage) is all Chardonnay — mineral, vibrant, and strikingly precise. An excellent ambassador for the grower Champagne movement.

Tarlant is a highly regarded grower Champagne house, and L'Aérienne Rosé is a prestige vintage cuvée. At 22 years old, the mousse will have softened but the complexity gains are profound — dried fruits, toast, oxidative depth. If stored properly, a genuinely extraordinary drinking experience.

Cazé-Thibaut is a small grower Champagne producer from the Marne Valley making vintage-dated wines. The 2018 Champagne vintage was warm and generous, producing wines of unusual richness for the region. The Millésimé is drinking well now with several years of evolution ahead.

Domaine Carneros is Taittinger's California joint venture, producing traditionally-made sparkling wines in the cool Carneros district. The Blanc de Noir is all Pinot Noir — pink-tinged, creamy, and delicious. Drink this non-vintage wine within the next few years for maximum freshness.

The 2021 Brut Rosé is one of Domaine Carneros's most popular cuvées — elegant Pinot-driven sparkling wine from the cool Carneros AVA. The 2021 California vintage was pristine and focused. Drinking beautifully now through 2030.

The Ultra Brut is Domaine Carneros's zero-dosage prestige cuvée — austere, food-friendly, and complex. The 2019 vintage was exceptional for California sparkling wine; this wine shows fine autolytic complexity alongside pure Carneros fruit. Drinking well now through 2032.

Ashes & Diamonds is one of Napa's most thoughtful producers, making mid-weight wines with French sensibility. Cabernet Franc 10 is floral, herbaceous, and structured — a stylistically distinctive Napa bottle. The 2023 vintage delivered freshness and elegance. Give it a year or two.

Hartford Family sources Zinfandel from old-vine parcels in the Russian River Valley. Winberrie Knolls delivers structured Zinfandel with cool-climate freshness that prevents jammy excess. The 2023 Sonoma vintage was outstanding. Hold this one; open the 2019 first — it's ready now.

Nickel & Nickel specializes in single-vineyard, unblended Cabernet Sauvignons. Branding Iron Vineyard in Oakville delivers concentrated, structured Cab with impressive aging potential. Note: your spreadsheet lists 'Braining Iron' — almost certainly a typo for 'Branding Iron.' Needs 3–5 years.

Heitz Cellar is one of Napa's most storied estates. Trailside Vineyard in Rutherford produces elegant, classic Cabernet with the appellation's signature dusty tannins and dark fruit. The 2019 vintage was exceptional throughout Napa — superb balance and aging potential. Entering its window now.

Martha's Vineyard is arguably Napa Valley's most historically important wine — the benchmark California Cabernet since the 1960s, known for its signature eucalyptus character. The 2019 is exceptional and will peak around 2030–2035. One of the cellar's true icons; handle with care.

Le Diamant is Vérité Estate's inaugural white wine — 100% Sauvignon Blanc from high-elevation volcanic micro-crus in Sonoma, inspired by Pessac-Léognan. A serious, age-worthy white in the Haut-Brion Blanc tradition. Three bottles at $175 market makes this the cellar's single largest white wine holding.

B.A. Theriot is one of Littorai's most celebrated single-vineyard Chardonnays, grown on marine-sediment soils of the Sonoma Coast. Complex, mineral, and built for aging — Littorai at its most ambitious. The 2023 vintage was excellent; give it 2–3 more years before opening.

Mays Canyon is a historic Russian River Valley vineyard and one of Littorai's most important parcels. The 2023 Sonoma vintage was exceptional — bright, pure, and deeply aromatic Pinot Noir. At $163 retail, this is a serious investment; give it 2–3 years before opening.

Wendling Vineyard in Alexander Valley is an unexpected site for Littorai — warmer than the Sonoma Coast parcels but yielding Pinot Noir of depth and richness. The 2023 shows the vintage's characteristic generosity. Two bottles allows for an early and a late drinking comparison.

Tortoniano is Michele Chiarlo's entry-level Barolo — Nebbiolo from the Serralunga d'Alba sub-zone, known for its powerful, austere style. The 2021 Barolo vintage was exceptional. Purchased at $18 vs. $50 market — but Barolo is not a short-term play. Cellar until at least 2027.

wines.varietal: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Malbec, Tannat, Petit Verdot
wines.summary: A commemorative bottling of Stags' Leap Winery's 125th anniversary — a Cabernet-dominant Bordeaux blend (81% Cab Sauv, 11% Merlot, 4% Malbec, 2% Tannat, 2% Petit Verdot) from Napa's exceptional 2018 vintage. Rated 95 by James Suckling. Purchased at $18 vs. $58 market: one of the stronger QPR bottles in the RNDC library cohort. Drinking well now.

Louis Jadot's Clos Saint-Jacques is sourced from one of Gevrey-Chambertin's most celebrated Premier Cru lieux-dits. The 2016 vintage produced beautifully structured wines: expect kirsch, cranberry, rose petal, and earthy depth with silky tannins and a long, precise finish. Rated 92-94 pts (WA). Best from 2026 through 2040.

Finca Adalgisa's 2018 Malbec from Lujan de Cuyo, Mendoza, is a classic example of Argentine Malbec. The excellent 2018 vintage conditions contributed to a wine with vibrant dark fruit, well-integrated tannins, and a balanced structure, making it enjoyable now and over the next few years.

Trimbach's Cuvee Frederic Emile is among the benchmark dry Rieslings of Alsace, sourced exclusively from the Geisberg and Osterberg grands crus. The 2012 vintage is drinking beautifully now: petrol, white peach, lemon curd, and crystalline minerality underpin a wine with decades of life ahead. This 1.5L magnum (93 pts) will evolve even more gracefully than the 750ml.

Domaine Berthet-Rayne's 2022 Châteauneuf-du-Pape is a rich, full-bodied red from the Southern Rhône, showcasing the ripeness and concentration typical of the vintage. Expect expressive aromas of dark berries, kirsch, garrigue herbs, and a hint of spice. This wine offers a structured palate with integrated tannins, promising excellent aging potential and a complex, lingering finish.

This Tokaj Oremus 2018 Aszú 5 Puttonyos is a classic Hungarian dessert wine, showcasing the intensity and complexity from noble rot in a well-regarded vintage. Expect a concentrated, honeyed wine with notes of dried apricot, orange marmalade, and a vibrant acidity that ensures balance and a very long finish.

Ultramarine is one of California's premier sparkling wine producers, and this 2021 Heintz Vineyard Rosé de Saignée from the Sonoma Coast is a benchmark expression. Expect fine, persistent bubbles with red berry fruit, bright acidity, and a creamy texture — a serious sparkling rosé with cellaring potential to 2027.

Black Ankle Vineyards' 2022 Domaine is a robust Red Wine from Frederick County, Maryland. Expect a fruit-forward and well-structured blend, showcasing the ripeness and character of the vintage, making it enjoyable in its youth with potential for further development.

wines.producer: Sister Farms (Burnt Hill x Old Westminster)
wines.summary: This is Suncatcher Rosé de Saignée, produced in collaboration by Sister Farms with Old Westminster and Burnt Hill. Expect a vibrant and refreshing rosé, crafted using the Saignée method, offering notes of red berries and a crisp finish ideal for youthful enjoyment.

wines.appellation: IGP Vi de la terra Mallorca
wines.varietal: Merlot, Prémsal blanc, Giró Ros, Macabeu, Riesling
wines.summary: A Mallorcan field blend from grapes grown at Es Racó d’Artà. Vinified in Provençal style with spontaneous fermentation and no added yeasts, consistent with the winery’s biodynamic approach. A characterful rosé suited to Mallorcan table food, acquired in remembrance of a sublime trip to Mallorca in October 2025.

Weingut Vollenweider's 2017 Kröver Steffensberg Riesling Spätlese from the Mosel region offers a classic German white wine profile. This vintage delivers vibrant acidity balanced by elegant sweetness, showcasing notes of ripe stone fruit, citrus, and a distinct minerality, making it enjoyable now or with further cellaring.

Calstar Cellars 2015 Sangiacomo Vineyard Pinot Noir from Sonoma Coast offers a classic expression of cool-climate Pinot Noir, showcasing bright red fruit, earthy undertones, and elegant structure from a strong vintage. Expect a wine with good balance and a graceful finish, ready to enjoy now or over the next few years.

Weingut Wasenhaus is a highly regarded German producer from Baden. The 2023 Möhlin Landwein, likely a Spätburgunder, offers vibrant red fruit, a touch of earthiness, and crisp acidity, characteristic of a fresh and approachable vintage from this esteemed estate.

The FM is Cornelissen's single-vineyard expression from the lower section (sottana) of the Feudo di Mezzo contrada in Passopisciaro, on Etna's north face at 580 metres. Despite the lower elevation — where you might expect bigger, more extracted wines — Feudo di Mezzo sottana produces wines of unusual delicacy: what Cornelissen himself calls 'Burgundian elegance and roundness.' The 2021 is 100% Nerello Mascalese from 40+ year old vines, fermented with indigenous yeasts on skins for 50 days and aged 18 months in neutral tanks before an equal stretch in bottle. Production is approximately 2,500 bottles.

Domaine Tempier's Bandol Rosé is one of the benchmarks of Provence — a structured, Mourvèdre-led blend (with Grenache, Cinsault, and Carignan) that ages far longer than most rosés and rewards patience. The Peyraud family's 2025 continues the estate's tradition of saline minerality, restrained red fruit, and a dry herbal finish that mirrors the garrigue of the Bandol hills. Drink now through 2030, with the wine gaining complexity over the first few years.

The Fledge & Co. is the experimental label of Maurgeux Nel, winemaker at Boplaas in Calitzdorp, Klein Karoo — a region better known for port-style fortifieds than table wine. The Niwatori no Ha is Souzão made dry and unoaked: a deliberate inversion of the grape's usual role, showing deep colour, bright acidity, and dark berry fruit without the fortification. Limited to 1,888 bottles. Drink young while the freshness holds.

wines.wine: Moulin à Vent Les Trois Roches
wines.summary: Pierre-Marie Chermette's 2023 Moulin à Vent Les Trois Roches is a classic example of Cru Beaujolais. Expect vibrant red fruit notes, floral hints, and a structured palate with a fresh acidity, typical of the balanced and expressive 2023 vintage. This wine offers enjoyable drinking in its youth but also possesses the potential for further development with a few years in the cellar.

The 2023 Willamette Valley is sourced from four northern sites — Amity Hills, Seven Springs, Björnson, and Eola Springs. It shows classic cool-climate tension: rose petal and cranberry aromatics, mouth-watering acidity, and fine-grained tannins. Nimble rather than weighty, it's immediately enjoyable but built to develop over the next several years.

wines.producer: R. Lopez de Heredia Viña Tondonia
wines.summary: R. Lopez de Heredia is an iconic, traditional Rioja producer known for its age-worthy wines. The 2012 Viña Tondonia Reserva is an elegant expression, characterized by dried red fruits, tertiary notes of leather, tobacco, and a refreshing acidity, offering complexity and a long finish. This vintage is entering its prime drinking window but promises further evolution.

Château d'Yquem is the world's most renowned sweet wine producer. The 2006 vintage was excellent, yielding a wine of incredible concentration and purity, with classic notes of honeyed apricot, marmalade, and a touch of botrytis spice, destined for decades of aging.

Finca Adalgisa's 2019 Malbec from Luján de Cuyo showcases the typical richness of Mendoza. Expect a medium to full-bodied red with concentrated dark fruit flavors like blackberry and plum, complemented by soft tannins and hints of vanilla or spice. This wine offers an approachable yet elegant expression of Argentine Malbec, suitable for enjoyment now or within the next few years.

Chermette's Les Garants comes from Fleurie's most prized granitic terroir (South-West facing, ~45yr vines) — RVF calls it 'Queen of Beaujolais.' The 2022 drew strong marks (RVF 93, Wine Enthusiast/James Suckling 92): blackcurrant, redcurrant, black raspberry fruit, floral-spicy nose, long finish. Age-worthy for Cru Beaujolais, peaking 3–6 years post-vintage.

Hofgut Falkenstein is celebrated for its traditional, expressive Mosel Rieslings, often showcasing a distinct sense of place. This 2024 Krettnacher Euchariusberg Spätlese, from a renowned vineyard, is expected to exhibit a vibrant interplay of delicate sweetness and razor-sharp acidity. It will offer pure fruit expression and possess significant aging potential.

Tessa Laroche farms roughly 12 hectares of organically certified Chenin on schist slopes beside Coulée de Serrant, in one of the Loire's two single-vineyard appellations. Native-yeast fermentation and élevage mostly in tank with some used cask give a dry, flinty, tightly structured white that is approachable young but built for two decades. Expect quince, green apple and honeycomb over crushed-stone minerality and a long, saline finish.

wines.producer: Les Errances (Warren Truchon et Maïté Perrocheau)
wines.wine: Quand fond la neige, où va le blanc ?
wines.summary: Warren Truchon and Maïté Perrocheau founded Les Errances in 2017 and now farm about five hectares organically around Rablay-sur-Layon in Anjou. This 100% Chenin from old vines is pressed directly to old barrels and raised on its lees for around 11 months with minimal sulfur, giving a dry, tense white with orchard fruit, lime and a faintly oxidative, honeyed edge. Bottled as Vin de France and made in small quantities; drinks well now and should hold a few years.

Hambledon is England's oldest commercial vineyard, planted on chalk in Hampshire's Meon Valley. The Classic Cuvée is a Chardonnay-led traditional-method blend with Pinot Noir and Meunier, aged a minimum of 35 months on lees and finished dry. Green apple, citrus blossom and salted-nut brioche ride on brisk chalky acidity; Decanter scored the current release 92 and JancisRobinson.com 17/20.

Château Paradis is an 80-hectare organic estate at Le Puy-Sainte-Réparade on the northern edge of Coteaux d'Aix, between Sainte-Victoire and the Luberon, run by Xavier and Odile Thieblin with the Tardieu family consulting. The 2025 estate rosé is Syrah-led with Grenache and a splash of Vermentino, showing pear, citrus and stone fruit with fresh acidity and a rounder, more generous texture than the pale-and-lean Provence norm. Best drunk young.

Fonscolombe is a historic estate at Le Puy-Sainte-Réparade north of Aix, producing organic Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence rosé from Syrah, Grenache, Carignan and Cabernet via short maceration and saignée. This specific 'Cuvée de la Reine' bottling could not be verified online, so appellation, blend and score are unconfirmed. Expect a dry, pale Provence rosé of stone fruit, red berries and grapefruit freshness, for drinking young.

Made from ungrafted, century-old Listán Blanco vines on volcanic soils in Tenerife's Valle de la Orotava, this wine is spontaneously fermented in concrete and aged about a year in foudre with no fining or filtration. The result is a linear, saline white with chalky minerality and citrus, wet-stone character; recent vintages of Palo Blanco have scored 96-98 from Wine Advocate (Luis Gutiérrez).

A big, rounded, generous Beaune from Domaine des Héritiers Louis Jadot's monopole Clos des Ursules (the '(H)' on the invoice): spicy cinnamon, clove and toast over vivid raspberry, red plum and mint, wrapped in fine-grained tannins. Rated 92-94 (Wine Advocate), 91-94 (Burghound), 95 (Wine Spectator), 96 (James Suckling); Wine Spectator recommends 2029-2047.

Les Damodes sits at the northern edge of Nuits-Saint-Georges, bordering Vosne-Romanée, and typically yields elegant, perfumed Pinot Noir. Rated 94 (Wine Advocate); a CellarTracker community note on this exact wine independently scored it 93. Now 15 years from vintage and should be drinking well; drink window is an estimate for the appellation/vintage, not a specific critic recommendation.

Chanlin is a Volnay premier cru farmed by Domaine Gagey, Jadot's own domaine holding (the '(G)' on the invoice). No vintage-specific critic score was found for 2017; CellarTracker community notes for nearby vintages (2013: 88, 2020: 90) cluster in line with Jadot's overall community average of 89.6, used here as an estimate. Expect the silky, red-fruited, earlier-drinking style typical of Volnay.

Montée de Tonnerre is one of Chablis's most highly regarded premier crus, a right-bank site adjoining the grand cru slope and known for stony, flinty intensity. Jadot's version is barrel-aged 10–12 months in 400L casks with partial malolactic, giving a taut, citrus-driven wine over Kimmeridgean minerality. No reliable critic score for this bottling was found; the drinking window is inferred from 2023 Chablis vintage guidance — a ripe, low-acid year whose structured premier crus open from 2026 and hold 8–12 years from vintage.

wines.wine: Pernand-Vergelesses Clos de la Croix de Pierre Blanc
wines.summary: Village-level Pernand-Vergelesses Chardonnay from the Clos de la Croix de Pierre climat (the red bottling from the same climat is classified premier cru; this white is not). Rated 93 (Jasper Morris): fresh mid-lemon fruit with floral and oak notes and chalky 'limestone pebble' minerality. Producer suggests it will develop in bottle for 5-10 years.

A dry, crisp Pinot Noir rosé from Domaine Clair-Dau, one of Jadot's historic domaine holdings in Marsannay. No critic or community score was found despite searching. Already 3 years from vintage - worth prioritizing for consumption soon rather than cellaring further.

Frémiets is one of Volnay's most respected premier crus, prized for structure and minerality relative to the commune's usual softness. Faiveley's 2018 offers an inviting bouquet of red berries, spice and a touch of oak, with silky tannins. Rated 93 (Wine Advocate); CellarTracker community average 92.

Les Porêts-Saint-Georges sits on Nuits-Saint-Georges' southern half, known for rich, structured Pinot Noir. Faiveley's 2018 shows plum confit and brandy-soaked black cherry accented by smoke, char and violet petals; rated 95 (Wine Enthusiast, Anna Lee C. Iijima). 2018 is a ripe, classic Côte de Nuits vintage, already approachable but built to age.

Village-level Chambolle-Musigny from Faiveley: brilliant garnet color, pretty woody and fruity nose, ripe cherry on the palate with present but unobtrusive tannins. Rated 89 from a single barrel-sample critic review (2023 not yet widely reviewed in bottle); 2023 is a lighter, more perfumed vintage in this commune.

Domaine Collotte's Marsannay Blanc, made from Chardonnay on the village's white-wine parcels. Wine-Searcher's aggregate across vintages sits at 89/100 from 5 critic reviews; a 2014 vintage was separately rated 90 by Wine Enthusiast (Roger Voss). Buttery and complex in style.

A dry, crisp Pinot Noir rosé, orange-pink in color, with clean aromas of red berry and tangerine plus secondary accents per a retailer tasting note on this vintage. Wine-Searcher's aggregate across vintages sits at 89/100 from 21 critic reviews, among the most consistently reviewed bottlings in Domaine Collotte's range.
Les Champsalomon is one of Domaine Collotte's flagship old-vine Marsannay lieux-dits. Wine-Searcher's aggregate across vintages sits at 89/100 from 22 critic reviews; savory and classic in style.

Les Boivins is a Marsannay lieu-dit farmed by Domaine Collotte from vines over 40-50 years old, known for seductive aroma, intensity and silky texture. Wine-Searcher's aggregate across vintages sits at 90/100 from 9 critic reviews, among the strongest in the domaine's Marsannay range.
Les Évocelles is a village-level Gevrey-Chambertin lieu-dit farmed by Domaine Collotte. A CellarTracker community note on this exact 2023 bottling scored it 89 points.

consumed.summary: Altanuta's Pinot Grigio from the Vicenza DOC sits in the eastern Veneto, where the variety produces crisp, mineral wines with stone fruit and a clean, dry finish. The 2021 vintage in the Veneto was warm and ripe. At five years old this is at the outer edge of its window — open soon.

Montlouis-sur-Loire faces Vouvray across the river, producing equally compelling Chenin Blanc at a fraction of the fame. François Chidaine is the benchmark producer of the appellation. 'Les Bournais' is dry, taut, and mineral. The 2019 vintage gave excellent concentration; drink through 2032.

Chapelle-Chambertin is a Grand Cru appellation in Gevrey-Chambertin. The 2004 Burgundy vintage was underrated but produced wines with real structure. At 22 years old and purchased for just $18, this wine is at or past its window. Open immediately — complexity is fading, not building.

Krontiras makes 'Cosmic Amber' as a skin-contact Torrontés — Argentina's aromatic white variety given the orange wine treatment. The result is textured, tannic, and savory with characteristic floral lift. Drink within a few years of release; these styles don't benefit from extended cellaring.

Pivot is Littorai's estate vineyard on the Sonoma Coast, farmed biodynamically by Ted Lemon. A benchmark site for cool-climate Pinot Noir — savory, mineral, and structured with remarkable depth. The 2023 is young and tightly wound; patience will be rewarded. Do not open before 2026.

Cour-Cheverny is the only AOC in the world that mandates Romorantin, an ancient Loire variety of great rarity. Domaine de Montcy's 'Licorne' showcases the variety's distinctive quince and waxy minerality. One of the most intellectually interesting bottles in this cellar.

consumed.varietal: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cab Franc, Petit Verdot
consumed.summary: Elivette is Spring Mountain Vineyard's flagship Bordeaux blend from their historic estate above St. Helena. At 25 years old in a 3-liter format (which aids longevity), this is a rare and important bottle. The 2001 scored 91 points and is approaching the outer edge of its window — open this year.

AIX Rose is one of Provence's most recognisable labels: pale-salmon, delicate, and precision-crafted from Grenache, Syrah, and Cinsault. The 2023 delivers white peach, wild strawberry, and Herbes de Provence with a clean mineral finish. This 1.5L magnum is ideal for the table; drink through 2027.

Planeta's Etna Bianco is made from Carricante grown on the volcanic soils of Sicily's Mount Etna. The 2017 shows the appellation's signature minerality — flint, citrus pith, white peach, and saline tension — with a long, focused finish. Scores 90 pts; drinking well now through 2028.

The 2019 Winberrie Knolls is the more mature expression of Hartford's Zinfandel program — now in a lovely drinking window with integrated fruit and emerging complexity. The 2019 California vintage showed excellent balance. Open this before the 2023; it's ready now.

Le Diamant is Vérité Estate's inaugural white wine — 100% Sauvignon Blanc from high-elevation volcanic micro-crus in Sonoma, inspired by Pessac-Léognan. A serious, age-worthy white in the Haut-Brion Blanc tradition. Three bottles at $175 market makes this the cellar's single largest white wine holding.
consumed.myNote: Clear; light gold color with green undertones. Expressive nose (peach, kiwi, Dragonfruit), palette, primarily lemon-lime with a distinct minerality and long finish

consumed.summary: The Calstar Cellars 2015 Sangiacomo Vineyard Pinot Noir showcases a refined expression from the renowned Sonoma Coast. The warm 2015 vintage typically yielded concentrated fruit with good structure, offering bright red fruit, savory notes, and a smooth finish that is well-integrated and ready to enjoy.
consumed.myNote:
Expressive nose, strawberry/red fruit leading into cooked fruit (intense almost reductive sweetness); palate leans sweet but is quite balanced; tannins are light but present, well integrated. Long and pleasurable finish

Overall: High intensity, moderate complexity, great balance, long finish, atypical vs other Pinot/SonomaPinot but enjoyable

consumed.appellation: Van Duzer Corridor AVA, Willamette Valley
consumed.summary: Johan Vineyards' 2023 Estate Pinot Noir is a fresh, vibrant expression of biodynamic winemaking from Oregon's Willamette Valley. Expect bright red fruit, subtle earthy notes, and a lively acidity, characteristic of a young Willamette Valley Pinot Noir. This wine offers approachable elegance for immediate enjoyment or short-term cellaring.
consumed.myNote:
Nose leads with barnyard and earthiness, followed by dark fruit (blackberries); palate matches the earthiness of the nose, leaner (acid-led) but well balanced; tannins are medium, really fine and well integrated
Overall: Medium + intensity, high complexity, medium finish, great balance, moderate typicity

consumed.summary: Enfield Wine Co.'s Foot Tread is typically a vibrant, medium-bodied red wine, often crafted from Trousseau using traditional methods. A recent vintage like 2022 would showcase bright red fruit, subtle earthy notes, and a refreshing acidity, reflecting the producer's focus on cool-climate expression and minimal intervention winemaking.

Chermette's 'Pierreux' (rocky) Brouilly comes from blue volcanic granite soils, producing Gamay of unusual density and mineral character. Brouilly is the largest of the ten Beaujolais crus. The warm 2022 vintage gives real structure; can age nicely to 2029.

Cantina del Pino is best known for its Barbaresco, but Franca Miretti's Barbera d'Asti Bricco Gallinetta is a standout in its own right — bright, juicy, and built around the grape's defining high acidity and deep ruby colour. The 2024 vintage shows ripe black cherry and plum with an earthy, peppery finish and the smooth, gripless texture that makes Barbera so food-friendly. A versatile everyday red that punches well above its price.

Weiser-Künstler is among the most compelling young estates in the Mosel, with Konstantin Weiser and Eva Künstler farming organically and coaxing wines of crystalline purity from their steep slate sites. This 2025 Riesling is an entry-level expression from the estate but carries the house hallmarks: bright citrus and white peach, pronounced minerality, and the lively acidity that defines great Mosel Riesling. Drink over the next few years while the fruit is fresh, though quality slate-based Riesling at this level invariably rewards a year or two of patience.

Winemaker John Lockwood's homage to the rugged vineyards of southern France, Club Catalanes is a Grenache-led field blend (with Cinsault and Carignan) grown across California. The 2023 shows wild strawberry and cranberry lifted by fresh acidity, with a whisper of garrigue and a light, juicy finish — textbook warm-climate Grenache kept honest by the other two varieties. Enfield's natural-leaning approach keeps things lively and low-intervention; drink over the next two to three years.

This natural wine is expected to deliver bright red fruit, floral notes, and a refreshing acidity, best enjoyed in its youth shortly after its anticipated 2025 release.

Domaine Tempier's Bandol rosé is among the most serious rosés in the world — Mourvèdre-dominant, structured, and built for the table rather than the pool. The 2024 received 93 points from Wine Advocate, Vinous, and Wine Spectator alike, with critics noting pomegranate, grapefruit, and ripe orchard fruit with exceptional freshness. Drink now through 2030.

consumed.summary: A red-slate parcel bottling from Klaus-Peter Keller, made feinherb (off-dry) rather than trocken — German insiders often rate it alongside the Grosses Gewächs bottlings at a fraction of the price. The 2025 is a fresh, early-release vintage; the residual sugar and racy acidity give it real aging potential despite being approachable young.

Finca Adalgisa's 2018 Malbec from Lujan de Cuyo, Mendoza, is a classic example of Argentine Malbec. The excellent 2018 vintage conditions contributed to a wine with vibrant dark fruit, well-integrated tannins, and a balanced structure, making it enjoyable now and over the next few years.

Frank Cornelissen's Susucaru Rosso from the 2024 vintage is a vibrant and natural red wine, typically showing bright red fruit, savory notes, and volcanic minerality. Expect a light-to-medium bodied wine with characteristic freshness and an authentic expression of Etna's unique terroir.

Thibaud Boudignon's 2024 Rosé de Loire offers a vibrant and refreshing experience. This early release rosé showcases the crisp acidity and delicate red fruit often found in quality Loire rosés, perfect for immediate enjoyment and ideal for warm weather.

Amity Vineyards' 2021 Eola-Amity Hills Pinot Noir is sourced from three estate sites including the historic Temperance Hill Vineyard. Low yields from the warm 2021 vintage produced a wine with smoky plum, wild cherry, and dusty brambly notes framed by bright acidity and chalky tannins. A textbook cool-climate Oregon Pinot at an honest price.

Littorai's Vin Gris is a pale, dry rosé pressed directly from Pinot Noir — no skin contact, pure and delicate. Ted Lemon's biodynamic Sonoma Coast vineyards produce bright, mineral fruit. The 2025 is the newest wine in the cellar; drink within a year or two of release.

consumed.summary: Marqués de Murrieta's Castillo Ygay Blanco Gran Reserva Especial is one of Rioja's great rarities — only 13 vintages released since 1917. The 1986 spent 21 years in oak and six more in cement before bottling in 2014, developing a deeply oxidative, sherry-adjacent character: marzipan, hazelnut, honey, and dried citrus, balanced by remarkably fresh, high acidity. A landmark of traditional-style white Rioja.

consumed.summary: Taittinger Comtes de Champagne Blanc de Blancs 2013 is a prestige cuvée crafted exclusively from Grand Cru Chardonnay, reflecting the elegance of one of Champagne's iconic houses. The 2013 vintage, while challenging, yielded a wine of remarkable freshness, precise acidity, and underlying complexity from extended lees aging. Expect a vibrant, mineral-driven profile with notes of white flowers, toasted brioche, and a very long, refined finish, promising excellent aging potential.

Littorai's Haven Chenin Blanc is one of California's most compelling examples of the variety — made by Ted Lemon, whose formative years were spent in the Loire Valley. Waxy, textured, and mineral with extraordinary longevity potential. A unique and important wine for the California white wine canon.

Best served slightly cool alongside food; drink for freshness over the next 2–3 years.

Littorai's Sonoma Coast Chardonnay draws from multiple biodynamic vineyards across the appellation for a complex, terroir-driven blend. Ted Lemon trained under Guy Roulot in Burgundy, and that influence is unmistakable. The 2024 is very young; give it 18 months before opening.

Vieilles vignes Pinot Noir from Marsannay, the northern gateway to the Côte de Nuits. Collotte is a quality-focused domaine producing honest village Burgundy. The warm 2023 vintage produced plush, approachable wines — drink from 2025 onward.

consumed.summary: Cruse Wine Company is one of California's most celebrated small producers, working with heritage varieties from old vineyards. The Tradition Rosé Sparkling is vibrant, complex, and uniquely Californian. Drink soon for maximum freshness — this is not a wine to cellar.

François Chidaine's 2022 Les Choisilles is a classic dry Montlouis-sur-Loire Chenin Blanc. Expect a wine with vibrant acidity, mineral depth, and a complex array of flavors including green apple, citrus, and hints of honey and wet stone, showcasing the fresh character of the vintage.

A blend of fruit from several Anderson Valley vineyards, Les Larmes is Littorai's more approachable, earlier-drinking Pinot Noir bottling relative to its single-vineyard wines.
